ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The diagram shows an object made up of 12 dice glued-together. The object is dipped into some colour so that the entire outside is coloured in this new colour. How many of the small dice will have exactly four faces coloured in?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a 12-cube polycube. On the left, I see a vertical 2-by-2 block of dice. From the lower-right cube of that block, a vertical column continues downward. From the bottom of that column, a one-cube-wide arm runs to the right and turns upward at the far right, ending in a two-cube-high pillar. Reasoning: When the whole object is dipped in colour, a face is not coloured exactly when it is glued to a neighbouring die. So a small die has exactly four coloured faces precisely when it has exactly two glued faces, i.e. exactly two neighbouring dice. In the left 2-by-2 block plus its downward column: the three non-junction cubes of the 2-by-2 block each touch exactly two neighbours; the lower-right junction cube of the 2-by-2 block touches three neighbours; the cubes in the downward continuation have exactly two neighbours. Thus this part contributes 5 dice with exactly two glued faces. For the bottom/right arm, all the cubes have exactly two neighbouring dice except the top cube of the right-hand pillar, which has only one neighbour. This contributes another 5 dice with exactly two glued faces. Therefore, 5 + 5 = 10 small dice have exactly four faces coloured in.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram as a 12-cube polycube: on the left there is a vertical 2-by-2 block, with a further vertical column continuing down from its lower-right cube; from the bottom of that column a one-cube-wide horizontal/turning arm runs to the right, ending in a two-cube-high pillar. Then reason by face contacts. For each small die, count how many full faces are glued to neighboring dice. A die has exactly four coloured faces precisely when it has exactly two glued faces. In the left 2-by-2-plus-column part, all but the lower-right cube of the 2-by-2 block have exactly two neighboring dice; that exceptional junction cube has three. Along the bottom/right arm, all cubes have exactly two neighboring dice except the top cube of the right-hand pillar, which has only one. Thus 10 of the 12 small dice have exactly two glued faces, so 10 dice have exactly four coloured faces.
